steps.title: New objects wait
steps.text: The incremental collector holds new objects in its young generation: the nursery, then threshold1 / 2 aging spaces. A young collection examines the oldest aging space and moves what survives into the old generation. At a threshold0 of 1,000 kB, the young generation holds 12 MB.

marks.note: The worker's objects sit in the nursery and aging lanes. Visited stays empty until the first young collection, at 12 MB.

steps.title: Every object is work
steps.text: json_loads models a worker that calls json.loads 60 times a loop. No result holds a cycle, so each object a collection examines is work that frees nothing.

marks.note: Survived, in violet, fills each bar: the collection examined objects still in use.
The same violet. Freed, in red, stays a sliver until shutdown.

steps.title: The legacy collector looks twice
steps.text: A gen 0 collection examines the nursery every threshold0 kB, here 1,000. At 12 MB, a gen 1 collection examines the survivors again before they reach the old generation.

marks.note: From 1 to 5 MB, gen 0 collections examine the objects the worker builds. The tall bar at 12 MB is the gen 1 collection examining all 1,145 again.

steps.title: The incremental collector looks once
steps.text: The incremental collector first examines an object when its aging space is the oldest: 12 MB after its allocation at this threshold0.

marks.note: At 12, 14 and 16 MB, young collections move the worker's objects from the aging lane into visited, an aging space at a time.
Three bars, at 12, 14 and 16 MB, examine each object once.

steps.title: Work per MB adds it up
steps.text: Work per MB divides each collector's work, shutdown's included, by the 21 MB the run allocates.

marks.note: 192 against 136: the legacy collector examined the worker's objects twice.

steps.title: The PEP's threshold0
steps.text: At the PEP's threshold0 of 2,000 kB, the young generation holds 24 MB and the 21 MB run ends first. The incremental collector examines nothing before shutdown.

marks.note: Both fall. The incremental collector's 82 is shutdown's work alone, and the legacy collector's run ends before its first gen 1.

steps.title: Gen 2 fits the run
steps.text: Lower threshold0 to 120 kB, and gen 1 collections come often enough for a gen 2 collection to fit. It examines the worker's objects a third time: 249 work per MB against 136.

marks.note: Gen 1 bars every 1.44 MB, and the gen 2 collection's tall bar at 16 MB.
One gen 2 collection for the legacy collector. The incremental collector runs no sweep.

steps.title: A longer aging generation
steps.text: Raise threshold1 to 20, and the aging generation holds 10 aging spaces. The young generation grows to 22 MB, past the run, and the incremental collector examines nothing again.

marks.note: The aging lane holds the worker's objects to the end, and visited stays empty.
